type_note: user-visible: two config keys change meaning, a policy key is added, and Nora can now be called into any voice channel on the server instead of one.
summary: 「喂 Nora」 works in every voice channel on the server, and what is said lands in that server's own room rather than in a room per channel.
details: Nora could previously only be spoken to in ONE voice channel, named in config as a guild/channel pair. Zone 42 has more than ten voice channels and gains more, so that list was one nobody could keep true — and a channel Nora was not configured for refused the join outright, with 'I can't join that voice channel'. The allow-list is now the SERVER: any voice channel on a listed server admits her, and adding a new one configures nothing.

A spoken utterance is now recorded in the server's ordinary text room — the one whose policy.toml entry says `voice = true` — instead of getting a conversation of its own. Voice is a surface of a room, not a room: a plan spoken aloud and the same plan typed land in one notebook, under one culture, behind one `persons` list. Adding a voice channel therefore cannot add a room.

Whether Nora answers ALOUD is now decided by how she was asked, not by which room she is in. A question typed into a room she also listens to by voice gets a text reply; a question spoken gets a spoken one. Before this the two were the same fact, because speech had its own room.

`[speech.tts] voice_channel_ids` is now `voice_guild_ids` and holds bare server ids. A guild/channel pair in it refuses to start, with the reason: the key changed meaning, and an entry silently truncated to its server half would widen the allow-list while looking like it still worked.

The wake service sends the SERVER id now, not a conversation id, so `VOICE_CHANNEL_ID` is no longer read by it. The audio-controller still reads it, as the channel a restart reconnects to when it has no saved state of its own.

On restart, Nora adopts whichever channel the audio-controller says it is actually in, rather than the one config names. Until now those were the same by construction; now that she can be moved, re-joining the configured channel would have dragged her back out of the room people were in.
limitations: A server with no room marked `voice = true` refuses speech with a 400 and records nothing. That is deliberate — the alternative is guessing a room and writing what somebody said into it — but it means the wake path stays silent after an upgrade until the operator adds the line. Two rooms in one server claiming `voice = true` refuses to start.

The voice channel a sentence was spoken in is no longer sent to Nora at all, only the server. It is optional provenance on her side and the field is left empty: only the audio-controller knows which channel it is connected to, and the audio seam between it and the wake service carries audio frames and a speaker id, nothing else. A trace can say which SERVER a sentence came from, not which channel.

Anyone in the server, in any of its voice channels, can now make Nora join them. That is the same reach the server's text room already grants, and who may actually TRIGGER her is still the room's `persons` list — an unlisted member is recorded and not answered, exactly as when typing.

One connection per server is Discord's own limit and is unchanged: while Nora is in one voice channel, a join from another is refused as a conflict, not a move. Nobody can pull her out of a channel she is already in.

Not exercised live. The three voice containers were healthy but deaf when this was written — the rooms they pointed at had just been removed from policy.toml — so the wake path has not been run end to end since the change. The suites covering it are green, including new ones pinning that any channel in a guild joins, that a typed turn in a voice-enabled room still replies as text, and that restart adopts the controller's real channel.

Superseded in part by 'voice-on-more-than-one-server' in this same unreleased set: the voice containers no longer read any server or channel id from the environment, and one of each serves every server. Read that fragment for the shipped shape.
reason: design/voice-channel/07 §12.2 (B15) reversed by the operator 2026-09-17; §13 had named the condition that would reopen it. Prompted by the 2026-09-17 cleanup, where two extra Discord rooms in one workspace cost 1953 messages, 11 fabricated notes and the whole culture table (DEC-105: a workspace holds at most one room per platform).
